subject: chemistry
title: Organic Reactions Adventure: Equations, Polymers, Esters
welcome_lead: Today you'll balance combustion, make a polymer and an ester.
meta_desc: GCSE Chemistry — balanced combustion equations, addition polymerisation of ethene to poly(ethene), and ester formation.
final_note: You learned how to balance combustion, how poly(ethene) is made, and how esters form from alcohols and acids.

concepts.def: Same number of each atom on both sides
Small molecule that joins to form a polymer
Long chain made by repeating monomers
Alkenes open C=C and join — no other product
Has a −COOH group, e.g. ethanoic acid CH3COOH
Sweet-smelling product of alcohol + carboxylic acid

walkthroughs.body_html:
CH4 + O2 → CO2 + H2O — but the atoms don't yet balance.

Balance H first: put a 2 in front of H2O. Now there are 4 O on the right and 2 on the left, so put a 2 in front of O2.

Final: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O. Check: 1 C, 4 H, 4 O each side. ✓

Many ethene monomers link together. The C=C bond opens and the carbons join end to end.

n C2H4 → −[CH2−CH2]−n. Only one product, no atoms lost — that's addition polymerisation.

Alcohol + carboxylic acid (with an acid catalyst) → ester + water.

Ethanol + ethanoic acid → ethyl ethanoate + water. Esters smell sweet and fruity — pear drops, nail polish remover, glue.
